on both lines as US growth in the biopharma's hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis treatments, Amvuttra (vutrisiran) and Onpattro (patisiran), slowed.
While Q3 sales of the two therapies rose 59% year-over-year to $1.15B, US TTR therapies revenue rose $99M. Of that amount, stocking and rebate adjustments were responsible for $27M.
However, US TTR demand growth of $81M from the quarter compares to $129M in Q2.
Amvuttra is responsible for the bulk—87.5%—of Alnylam's product sales.
Revenue was also boosted in the quarter by a one-time milestone payment of $300M from a Roche

Although Alnylam's royalty revenue increased ~105% YoY to ~$94.7M, the company also pays tiered royalties to Sanofi on Amvuttra sales. Given global sales growth of the treatment, a 30% royalty rate will apply once sales hit $1.5B.
Amvuttra sales growth negatively impacted cost of goods sold in the quarter as it rose to 28% of product sales from 23.2%.
Alnylam maintained its 2026 guidance, with total product revenues projected at $4.7B-$5.1B. Revenue consensus is $5.48B. TTR net product revenue is seen at $4.2B-$4.5B.

title: Alnylam falls despite earnings beats as US Amvuttra, Onpattro sales growth slows
